candidate.content: In ALFWorld pick-and-place tasks where the target object is not immediately visible, prioritizing inspection of open horizontal surfaces (e.g., countertops) before opening closed storage receptacles can lead to rapid target acquisition. In this instance, visiting two open countertops sequentially resulted in finding the target plate on the second surface without needing to interact with any closed containers.
candidate.scope: ALFWorld environments containing both open horizontal surfaces and closed storage receptacles; specifically applies to the initial search phase for a target object that may be located on an open surface.

direct_grounding.semantic_fact: The agent visited countertop_1 (an open horizontal surface) and observed multiple items (apple, dishsponge, potatoes), but the target plate was not present.
The agent subsequently visited countertop_2 (another open horizontal surface) and observed the target item 'plate_2' among other objects.
The agent successfully took 'plate_2' from countertop_2, completing the acquisition phase after only two candidate inspections and three total actions.

minimal_global_context: The task required cleaning a plate, implying the need to first locate and acquire a plate object.
The environment contained numerous closed storage receptacles (cabinets, drawers, fridge, etc.) which were not inspected during this trajectory.
The strategy involved checking open surfaces first, aligning with the hypothesis that open surfaces are higher-priority candidates for immediate visibility.
